title: WattEV Tesla Semi Order Leads May 2026 EV Charging News
metaTitle: WattEV 370 Semis, Lexus TZ, VW ID Cross, ANSI Safety
metaDescription: May 6 2026 EV news: WattEV's 370 Tesla Semi order, Lexus TZ 3-row reveal, VW ID Cross spotted, BYD Datang 30K orders, ANSI fire-safety EV charger standards.
content:
Introduction

Wednesday, May 6, 2026 brings a news cycle organized around several converging fronts: the largest single Tesla Semi order in California history, an imminent flagship Lexus three-row electric SUV reveal, the final pre-launch testing of Volkswagen's first true entry-level EV, the staggering Chinese pre-order response to BYD's new Blade Battery 2.0 flagship, and a quiet but consequential standards-body decision on fire-safety protocols for EV charging installations in older buildings. WattEV announced yesterday that it will deploy 370 Tesla Semi trucks across Northern and Central California in a deal valued at approximately 100 million dollars, the largest single electric-truck order in California history, with more than 300 of the trucks bound for service at the Port of Oakland and the first 50 deliveries scheduled for later this year. Toyota will unveil the new Lexus TZ luxury three-row electric SUV on May 7, with 338-to-420-horsepower output, an estimated 320-mile range, and pricing expected to start near 60,000 dollars when it reaches U.S. showrooms in late 2026 or early 2027. Volkswagen's first entry-level ID. Cross small electric SUV has been spotted undisguised in final-stage testing ahead of its summer debut at a starting price of approximately 28,000 euros, with a 52-kilowatt-hour NMC option delivering a 271-mile WLTP range. BYD's new Datang flagship three-row electric SUV, unveiled at the Beijing Auto Show, attracted more than 30,000 confirmed pre-orders in its first 24 hours at pricing between 36,500 and 47,000 dollars, leveraging the company's Blade Battery 2.0 and Flash Charging architecture for a 590-mile range and a five-minute fast-charge time. And the American National Standards Institute Electric Vehicles Standards Panel has reclassified several fire-protection items as high-priority gaps in its April 2026 progress report, with the central focus on the need for new fire-safety standards for EV charging hardware installed inside older building structures that were not originally engineered for the thermal risks associated with high-power electrical loads. For Los Angeles property owners, these stories collectively confirm that the heavy-duty fleet electrification market is now executing at scale, the luxury and mainstream EV portfolios continue to expand rapidly, and the technical safety practices for residential and commercial charging in older properties are about to come under sharper standards-body scrutiny. WattEV Orders 370 Tesla Semis in $100 Million California Electric-Freight Deployment

WattEV announced on May 5 that it will deploy 370 Tesla Semi trucks across Northern and Central California in the largest single electric-truck order in state history, a deal valued at approximately 100 million dollars with more than 300 of the trucks bound for service at the Port of Oakland and the first 50 deliveries scheduled to begin later this year. According to WattEV's GlobeNewswire release, the deployment will be supported by new WattEV truck-charging stations at the Port of Oakland and in Fresno, both equipped with Tesla's Megawatt Charging System hardware capable of delivering approximately 300 miles of range in 30 minutes, and additional depots are under development for Stockton this year and Sacramento breaking ground later in 2026. The Northern and Central California network will extend WattEV's existing footprint of six operational depots in Southern California and connect the I-5 and I-580 freight corridors that move goods between the Bay Area, Central Valley, and the Los Angeles basin.

The WattEV deployment is highly relevant to Los Angeles industrial property owners because the Northern and Central California depot network operates as the upstream half of a single statewide freight system that converges on the Port of Long Beach and the Inland Empire warehouse cluster, and the validation of MCS-class megawatt charging at port-and-corridor sites confirms the commercial readiness of the depot model. Building on the freight-charging dynamics we covered in our recent post on the Pilot-Tesla Megacharger summer launch and the CATL six-minute Shenxing battery, the practical implication for Los Angeles industrial property owners along the I-710, I-110, I-5, and I-15 freight corridors is that megawatt-class fleet charging is now a near-term commercial reality, and properties positioned to host depot or megacharger sites should engage with LADWP service planning early in the project lifecycle. Shaffer Construction provides the electrical load studies and full commercial EV charger installation services required to specify, permit, and construct depot-scale fleet charging that meets MCS and Megacharger requirements.

Lexus TZ Three-Row Luxury Electric SUV Unveiling Set for May 7

Toyota will unveil the new Lexus TZ luxury three-row electric SUV on May 7 at 10:30 AM Japan Standard Time, equivalent to the evening of May 6 in U.S. Pacific Time, with the new model targeting the premium three-row segment alongside the Hyundai IONIQ 9, Kia EV9, Volvo EX90, and Mercedes EQS SUV. According to Car and Driver, the TZ will share its underlying platform with the upcoming Toyota Highlander EV and arrive in two power configurations of 338 horsepower for the TZ 450e and 420 horsepower for the TZ 550e, with an estimated 320-mile range, an expected starting price near 60,000 dollars, and U.S. customer deliveries beginning in late 2026 or early 2027. The TZ is expected to be assembled at Toyota's Kentucky facility alongside the Highlander EV, which would qualify the model for federal commercial-clean-vehicle credits and certain state purchase incentives.

The Lexus TZ is meaningful for Los Angeles luxury-vehicle buyers because Lexus operates one of the strongest premium retail and service networks in Greater Los Angeles, with significant footprints in Beverly Hills, Calabasas, Santa Monica, Glendale, Pasadena, and the South Bay. Building on the Lexus electrification themes we covered in our post on the Lexus ES native NACS launch and the 300,000 EV lease returns, the practical implication for Los Angeles luxury homeowners is that the TZ joins the ES, RX, and upcoming additional Lexus EV models as part of a fully fleshed-out lineup that supports 11.5-kilowatt Level 2 home charging on a standard 48-amp dedicated circuit. Shaffer Construction handles the full residential EV charger installation scope including main-panel evaluations, NEC 2023 load calculations, dedicated 240-volt circuit installation, and permit submission to the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety.

Volkswagen ID. Cross Spotted Undisguised Ahead of Summer Launch at €28,000 Starting Price

Volkswagen's new ID. Cross compact entry-level electric SUV has been spotted undisguised in final-stage road testing ahead of its planned summer 2026 debut at a starting price of approximately 28,000 euros for the European market. According to Volkswagen Newsroom, the ID. Cross will sit below the ID.4 in Volkswagen's lineup as the EV equivalent of the popular T-Cross gasoline crossover, with two battery options of a 37-kilowatt-hour LFP pack and a 52-kilowatt-hour NMC pack delivering up to 271 miles of WLTP range, a 13-inch central infotainment display, an 11-inch driver-cluster display, and a 22-liter front trunk. While the ID. Cross is not currently planned for the U.S. market, the platform and the underlying cost-down trajectory directly inform Volkswagen's eventual U.S. entry-level EV roadmap.

The ID. Cross is meaningful for Los Angeles property owners because the broader European entry-level EV pivot continues to validate the sub-30,000-dollar mainstream-priced mass-market EV thesis that is now consolidating across every major automaker. Building on the broader affordability themes we covered in our post on the Rivian-Caruso Los Angeles partnership and the Volkswagen ID. Polo $29,000 debut, the practical implication for Los Angeles homeowners is that the residential Level 2 charger installation pipeline will continue to widen as mass-market EV pricing converges on the gasoline-vehicle equivalent. Stacking the federal 30C tax credit, the LADWP residential rebate, and the new South Coast AQMD Resiliency Program funding remains the most efficient way to lower the all-in cost of installation. BYD Datang Flagship EV SUV Records 30,000 Orders in 24 Hours with 5-Minute Charging

BYD's new Datang flagship three-row electric SUV, unveiled at the 2026 Beijing Auto Show, attracted more than 30,000 confirmed pre-orders in its first 24 hours at pricing between 250,000 and 320,000 yuan, equivalent to approximately 36,500 to 47,000 dollars, with dealer reports suggesting reservations may have climbed to 60,000 within 48 hours. According to CarNewsChina, the Datang is more than 5,200 millimeters in length, larger than both the Hyundai IONIQ 9 and the Kia EV9, and is built on BYD's Blade Battery 2.0 architecture combined with the company's Flash Charging system to deliver 950 kilometers of CLTC-rated range and a five-minute fast-charge time at compatible high-power stations. While the Datang is currently a China-market product, the underlying battery and charging technology is highly likely to migrate to BYD's export-market vehicles over the coming product cycles.

The BYD pre-order surge and the Blade Battery 2.0 architecture are relevant to Los Angeles charging deployment because the global validation of five-minute fast-charging at 950-kilometer-range vehicles confirms that megawatt-class passenger-vehicle DC fast charging is moving from a technology demonstration to a deployable site specification. Building on the next-generation battery and charging dynamics we covered in our post on the CATL six-minute Shenxing third-generation battery and the Pilot-Tesla Megacharger summer launch, the practical implication for Los Angeles commercial property owners is that the high-power site specifications established today will need to remain upgradeable to support charge rates well above the current 350-to-600-kilowatt class as next-generation passenger vehicles arrive. Shaffer Construction performs the electrical load studies required to specify upgradeable transformer, switchgear, and conductor architectures that anticipate the future charge-rate progression.

ANSI Reclassifies EV Charger Fire-Safety Standards for Older Buildings as High Priority

The American National Standards Institute Electric Vehicles Standards Panel released its April 2026 Gaps Progress Report and reclassified several safety and infrastructure issues from medium to high priority, with the central focus on the identified need for new fire-protection standards for EV charging installations within older building structures that were not originally engineered for the thermal risks associated with high-power electrical loads. According to ANSI's April 2026 EVSP update, the gaps include thermal-risk modeling for residential garages and basements in pre-1990s construction, ventilation and detection requirements for parking-structure charger installations, and battery-thermal-event response protocols for charger installations near the building envelope. The high-priority designation is expected to accelerate parallel work at the National Fire Protection Association, Underwriters Laboratories, and state-level building-code bodies including the California Building Standards Commission.

The ANSI prioritization is highly relevant to Los Angeles property owners because the city's building stock includes a substantial inventory of single-family residences, multi-family buildings, mixed-use properties, and commercial structures that predate the modern era of EV charger installations and that may require additional electrical, thermal, or ventilation provisions to safely host higher-amperage Level 2 hardware. Building on the permitting and policy themes we covered in our post on why permitting policy and smart design matter for faster EV charger deployment in Los Angeles, the practical implication for Los Angeles homeowners and commercial property owners is that engaging a licensed electrical contractor experienced with the Los Angeles Department of Building and Safety permitting process is the most reliable path to a code-compliant, safe, and properly inspected installation. Shaffer Construction performs the electrical load studies and main-panel evaluations required to identify the structural, thermal, and electrical-service constraints unique to older Los Angeles properties and to specify charger installations that meet current code and emerging fire-safety best practices.

Conclusion

The news cycle of May 6, 2026 documents an EV market that is now executing on multiple fronts simultaneously across the heavy-duty freight, luxury passenger, mainstream affordable, and global flagship segments while the underlying technical-safety standards continue to mature. WattEV's 370-truck Tesla Semi order is the largest single California electric-freight deployment to date and validates megawatt-class depot charging as a near-term commercial reality. The Lexus TZ luxury three-row reveal scheduled for May 7 brings Toyota's premium brand fully into the segment dominated by Hyundai, Kia, Volvo, and Mercedes. Volkswagen's ID. Cross at a 28,000-euro starting price confirms the global pivot toward sub-30,000-dollar mainstream EVs. BYD's Datang 30,000-order pre-launch surge and the Blade Battery 2.0 Flash Charging architecture validate megawatt-class passenger-vehicle charging as a deployable specification. And the ANSI prioritization of fire-safety standards for EV charging in older buildings is an important reminder that the technical-safety practices for residential and commercial charging in Los Angeles's diverse building stock are about to come under sharper standards-body scrutiny. For Los Angeles property owners, the cumulative signal is that the next eight weeks before the federal 30C tax credit expires on June 30 represent the most economically favorable installation window of the year, and projects that begin permitting in the next two weeks are the projects most likely to capture the full credit alongside available LADWP residential and commercial rebates and the new South Coast AQMD Resiliency Program funding.
